name: PixiTween Director S03b: director agent (brief to storyboard to composition), listener, create-film route, panels
description: Turns a product photo and a typed or spoken brief into a storyboard (Spark strict json_schema), then builds every scene through the S3a authoring tools (parallel tool calls, repair loop, deterministic fallbacks), exposes runDirector(filmId) and the POST /api/films route (handlers/films.ts), a listener for voice memos, a DIRECTOR_FAKE development mode, and the NewFilm and Storyboard panels. Excludes art (S4), review (S5), chat (S6) and generate-mode clips (S7).

userStories.title: Spark storyboard JSON schema and normaliseStoryboard (server/agent/storyboard.ts part 1)
userStories.description: As a director author, I want a strict schema for Spark and a deterministic normaliser so that whatever the model returns becomes a valid Storyboard.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-03-brief-to-composition/design.md sections 5.9 (normalisation rules) and 4.3 (storyboard example), shared/storyboard.ts (storyboardSchema, MAX_GENERATE_SCENES) and fixtures/seed/spark-storyboard-response.json.

Create fixtures/s03b/storyboard-spark-raw.json: a hand-made raw Spark answer {title, palette, scenes: [...]} with 4 scenes whose ids are model-style ('scene-1-hero-reveal'), every scene having all nine fields (id, durationSec, intent, shotType, camera, layersWanted, text, mode, modeReason); scenes 2, 3 and 4 have mode 'generate'; scene 1 text is 'Slow mornings' and the others ''; one palette entry is 'red' (invalid) and one '#F5E6D3' (upper case).

Create server/agent/storyboard.ts exporting SPARK_STORYBOARD_SCHEMA (the hand-written strict JSON schema of design 5.9: type object, additionalProperties false, required title, palette, scenes; each scene requires all nine fields; shotType, camera, layersWanted items and mode are enums; no numeric bounds) and normaliseStoryboard(raw: unknown, o: {aspect: Aspect; title?: string}): Storyboard following design 5.9 exactly (ids s1..sN assigned by code; title trimmed to 80 and o.title used when the model's is empty; palette lower-cased, invalid hex dropped, defaults ['#111827', '#f59e0b'] when none left, at most 6; durationSec clamped to [2, 8] and rounded to 0.1; text '' -> undefined and trimmed to 120; layersWanted de-duplicated with 'bg' always present and 'product' added unless shotType is 'lifestyle'; generate kept for the first MAX_GENERATE_SCENES scenes, the rest demoted to 'motion' with modeReason + ' (demoted: at most 2 generate scenes)' truncated to 240; estCredits 25 for generate and absent for motion; aspect forced to o.aspect; top-level durationSec = sum of scene durations).

The function throws StoryboardError (export the class; message names the first failing field) when the result still fails storyboardSchema, except that a total above 30 s is first scaled down proportionally (each scene at least 2 s) before validation.

Create server/agent/storyboard.test.ts: normalising the fixture gives scene ids s1..s4, the palette ['#f5e6d3'] plus nothing invalid, scenes 2 and 3 generate with estCredits 25 and scene 4 demoted to motion with the suffix in modeReason, scene 1 text 'Slow mornings' and others undefined, every scene durationSec within [2, 8]; a raw storyboard whose scenes sum to 40 s is scaled to at most 30 s; a missing scenes array throws StoryboardError naming 'scenes'; every property name of SPARK_STORYBOARD_SCHEMA's scene object exists in shared/storyboard.ts's sceneSchema shape (assert by key comparison) and every required key is listed in `required`.
acceptanceCriteria: Normalising fixtures/s03b/storyboard-spark-raw.json yields scene ids s1..s4, keeps scenes 2 and 3 as generate (the cap of 2, estCredits 25 each) and demotes scene 4 to motion with the suffix ' (demoted: at most 2 generate scenes)'
A raw storyboard whose scene durations sum to 40 s is scaled so the normalised total is at most 30 s with every scene at least 2 s
SPARK_STORYBOARD_SCHEMA lists all nine scene keys under `required` and sets additionalProperties false at both levels
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: planStoryboard: one Spark call, strict schema, photo, repair retry, cost
userStories.description: As a director, I want a reliable storyboard call so that a bad model answer is repaired or rejected cleanly instead of breaking the film.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-03-brief-to-composition/design.md sections 5.9 and 5.11, server/agent/storyboard.ts, server/agent/prompts/director.ts, shared/ports.ts (MetaClients, ChatResponse) and server/pricing.ts (priceSpark).

In server/agent/storyboard.ts add planStoryboard(o: {ctx: ToolCtx; film: FilmState; model: string; productJpeg?: Buffer}): Promise<Storyboard>. It builds messages with buildStoryboardMessages, calls ctx.meta.spark.chat({model, messages, response_format: {type: 'json_schema', json_schema: {name: 'storyboard', strict: true, schema: SPARK_STORYBOARD_SCHEMA}}}), records cost with ctx.ledger.add(film.id, model, `${in} in / ${out} out tokens`, priceSpark(model, in, out)) from response.usage (skip when usage is absent), emits ctx.emit({type: 'agent.turn', backend: 'spark', ms, calls: 0}), parses response.content as JSON and normalises.

Failure handling: a MetaApiError with status 400 while a photo is attached is retried once without the photo (emit an 'error' event {where: 'storyboard', message: 'retrying without the product photo'}); invalid JSON or a normalise/validation error triggers ONE repair call whose messages append the assistant content and a user message `Your JSON was invalid: <message>. Return the corrected JSON only.`; a second failure throws StoryboardError.

Create server/agent/plan.test.ts with makeTestFilm and makeFakeMeta({sparkScript}) (ChatResponse items {content, toolCalls: [], usage: {promptTokens: 1000, completionTokens: 1200}, ms: 5, model}): a valid answer returns a Storyboard with ids s1.. and the film's aspect; the first request carries response_format.json_schema.strict true and an image_url part when productJpeg is given (inspect meta.calls); an invalid answer followed by a valid one makes exactly 2 spark.chat calls and the second request's last message starts 'Your JSON was invalid'; two invalid answers throw StoryboardError after 2 calls; a fake spark client that throws MetaApiError(400) on the first call when an image is attached succeeds on the second call without the image and emits an error event; the ledger total after one call equals priceSpark(model, 1000, 1200) within 1e-9 and exactly one cost event is emitted.
acceptanceCriteria: A valid answer after one call returns a Storyboard and the first spark.chat request has response_format type 'json_schema' with strict true
An invalid answer then a valid one results in exactly 2 spark.chat calls, the second ending with a user message starting 'Your JSON was invalid'
After one call the ledger total equals priceSpark(model, 1000, 1200) and exactly one 'cost' event exists (no double counting)
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: buildScene: the per-scene tool loop with repair and stall detection
userStories.description: As a director, I want a bounded tool loop per scene so that parallel calls, errors and stalls are all handled without crashing.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-03-brief-to-composition/design.md section 5.10, server/tools/registry.ts (allTools, runTool), server/llm/messages.ts (assistantMessageFrom, toolResultMessage), server/agent/prompts/director.ts and fixtures/seed/spark-tool-loop-turns.json.

Create server/agent/build-scene.ts: export const EDIT_ONLY_TOOLS = ['removeLayer','reorderLayer','removeScene','swapScenes','setSceneDuration'] and buildScene(o: {ctx: ToolCtx; backend: LlmBackend; scene: Scene; canvas: {width, height, aspect}; palette: string[]; product: {assetId, width, height}; maxTurns?: number}): Promise<{turns: number; calls: number; ok: number; failures: string[]; stalled: boolean}>.

Loop (max 6 turns): tools = allTools() minus EDIT_ONLY_TOOLS; messages start with the system prompt from buildScenePrompt (toolNames = tools' names) and a user message JSON.stringify of the scene brief; each turn result = backend.chatWithTools(messages, tools, {parallelHint: true}); emit ctx.emit({type: 'agent.turn', backend: backend.id, ms: result.ms, calls: result.toolCalls.length}); record cost from result.usage with ctx.ledger when it has promptTokens and completionTokens; stop when toolCalls is empty; otherwise run every call in order with runTool(ctx, name, args), push assistantMessageFrom(result) then one toolResultMessage per call (the ToolResult JSON, including the error text); count successes.

Stop with stalled true after two consecutive turns that had tool calls but zero successes. A tool failure never throws out of buildScene; a backend exception is caught, pushed to failures, and ends the loop.

Create server/agent/build-scene.test.ts with makeTestFilm and makeFakeBackend: a film prepared with scene s1 (use the pure API + ctx.films.commit) and the product asset registered; script A: turn 1 returns six correct calls (addLayer bg shape fill '#111827', addLayer product image with the product assetId, addLayer headline text 'Slow mornings', setKeyframes {layerId:'s1:headline', prop:'opacity', keys:[[0,0],[0.6,1]], ease:'easeOut'}, setKeyframes product scale, setCamera s1 pan), turn 2 is {content:'DONE'}: result ok 6, turns 2, the stored composition has the three layers with ids s1:bg, s1:product, s1:headline and 6 tool.call events with ok true; script B built from the seed turn: its first turn calls setKeyframes with layerId 'headline' (a real failure) after the three addLayer calls, then a second turn repairs with layerId 's1:headline': failures has one entry, the second turn's tool results given to the backend contain the text 'Did you mean s1:headline?' (inspect the messages the fake backend received by wrapping it), final ok count 6; script C: three consecutive turns of only invalid calls give stalled true after 2 and turns 2; script D: a backend that always returns one valid call stops at 6 turns; the tool list passed to the backend contains none of EDIT_ONLY_TOOLS.
acceptanceCriteria: Script A produces ok 6 over 2 turns and the stored composition contains s1:bg, s1:product and s1:headline
In script B the failed setKeyframes (layerId 'headline') is fed back with 'Did you mean s1:headline?' and the repaired call succeeds, ending with 6 successful calls
Two consecutive all-failure turns set stalled true and end the loop; the tool list given to the backend never includes removeLayer, reorderLayer, removeScene, swapScenes or setSceneDuration
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: runDirector(filmId): orchestration, statuses, failure handling
userStories.description: As an owner, I want one entry point that takes a film from 'new' to 'ready' (or 'failed') so that the route handler and later steps just call runDirector.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-03-brief-to-composition/design.md sections 3.1, 5.9-5.11, 7 and 8, server/http/deps.ts (AppDeps, makeToolCtx), server/llm/router.ts (pickBackend) and the S3b modules created so far.

Replace the S2 stub in server/agent/director.ts: export createDirector(deps: AppDeps, o?: {backend?: LlmBackend; model?: string; delayMs?: number}) returning {runDirector(filmId): Promise<void>; isRunning(filmId): boolean}, bindDirector(deps) (stores a module-level director built with createDirector(deps)) and `export async function runDirector(filmId: string): Promise<void>` that delegates to the bound director (throws Error('director not bound') if bindDirector was never called).

Flow of one run (design 3.1): refuse a second concurrent run for the same film id; ctx = deps.makeToolCtx(filmId); film = await deps.films.get(filmId); set status 'planning' (films.update + ctx.emit film.status); productJpeg = resizeFit(await deps.assets.read(film.brief.productAssetId), 768, 'jpeg') (skip on failure); storyboard = await planStoryboard(...); films.update({storyboard, title}); ctx.emit director.storyboard; initFilmComposition; status 'building'; for each scene: buildScene (backend = o.backend ?? pickBackend('build')) then ensureSceneBasics; status 'ready' (films.update + emit).

Failure handling: StoryboardError or any unexpected exception sets status 'failed', emits {type: 'error', where: 'director', message} and resolves (never rejects); a scene whose buildScene reports stalled or zero ok calls emits an 'error' warning event {where: 'build-scene', message: `scene <id> filled with defaults`} and continues; the in-memory running set is always cleared in a finally block.

Create server/agent/director.test.ts with makeTestFilm (film with brief text and the product asset), makeFakeMeta({sparkScript: [storyboard answer built from fixtures/s03b/storyboard-spark-raw.json]}) and makeFakeBackend scripts that build each scene correctly (build the script in the test from the normalised storyboard): the final film status is 'ready', the stored composition has all scenes with bg and product layers and validates, events appear in the order film.status planning, director.storyboard, film.status building, agent.turn..., film.status ready, the number of stored versions is greater than 3 * 6, ledger total > 0 for the fake usage; a backend that returns no tool calls at all still ends 'ready' with bg/product/headline defaults from ensureSceneBasics and one error warning per scene; two invalid storyboard answers end with status 'failed', an error event and a resolved promise; calling runDirector twice at once on one film runs the work once (assert spark.chat calls); runDirector without bindDirector rejects with 'director not bound'.
acceptanceCriteria: A scripted successful run ends with film status 'ready' and every scene containing bg and product layers, with events ordered film.status planning, director.storyboard, film.status building, ..., film.status ready
A backend that never returns tool calls still yields a playable film (defaults from ensureSceneBasics) and one 'error' warning per scene
Two invalid storyboard answers end with status 'failed' plus an error event and the returned promise resolves
`npm run typecheck` passes
`npm test` passes (offline, no network)
`npm run lint` passes

userStories.title: POST /api/films input parsing and validation (handlers/films-input.ts)
userStories.description: As a user, I want clear errors when my upload is wrong so that I can fix it immediately.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-03-brief-to-composition/design.md section 5.12 (fields, limits, error codes), server/media/image.ts (imageSize) and the S2 stub server/http/handlers/films.ts.

Create server/http/handlers/films-input.ts: type CreateFilmInput = {product: {bytes: Buffer; mime: 'image/png'|'image/jpeg'|'image/webp'}; brief?: string; audio?: {bytes: Buffer; mime: string}; aspect: Aspect; title?: string}; class InputError {status: 400|413|415|429; code: string; message: string}; parseCreateFilm(body: Record<string, unknown>, o: {maxBytes: number}): Promise<CreateFilmInput> taking the object returned by Hono's c.req.parseBody() (File objects for files).

Rules in this order: `product` must be a File (code product_required, 400); its mime is decided by magic bytes (PNG 89504E47, JPEG FFD8, WEBP 'RIFF....WEBP'), not by the client (unsupported_media, 415); bytes over o.maxBytes -> too_large 413; exactly one of `brief` and `audio` (brief_or_audio 400 when both or neither); brief trimmed, longer than 2000 characters -> brief_too_long 400, empty after trimming -> brief_or_audio; audio mime must start with audio/ or be video/webm (unsupported_media 415) and bytes <= o.maxBytes; aspect default '16:9', anything else not in the three -> bad_aspect 400; title trimmed and cut to 80.

Create server/http/handlers/films-input.test.ts building bodies with File objects from the seed (mug-product.png, brief-16k.wav): a valid typed brief parses with aspect '16:9'; a valid audio brief parses; each error code above is produced by one test (product missing; a text file named x.png rejected as unsupported_media by its magic bytes; a 2 KB product with maxBytes 1024 -> too_large; both brief and audio; neither; a 2001-character brief; aspect '4:3'); a title of 100 characters is cut to 80.
acceptanceCriteria: A text file named product.png is rejected with code unsupported_media and status 415 because its magic bytes are not an image
A body with both `brief` and `audio`, or with neither, is rejected with code brief_or_audio and status 400
A valid typed brief parses with aspect '16:9' and a 100-character title is cut to 80

userStories.title: registerFilmsRoutes: POST /api/films creates the film and starts the director
userStories.description: As a user, I want to submit a photo and a brief and get a film id straight away while the director works in the background.
steps: Read docs/hackathon/steps/step-03-brief-to-composition/design.md sections 3.1 (steps 1) and 5.12-5.13, server/http/handlers/films.ts (the S2 stub), server/http/handlers/films-input.ts, server/listener.ts, server/agent/director.ts and server/http/deps.ts.

Replace the stub body of server/http/handlers/films.ts, keeping the exports STUB_OWNER and registerFilmsRoutes(app, deps): register POST /api/films (the passcode middleware already ran): parseBody -> parseCreateFilm (maxBytes from loadEnv().MAX_UPLOAD_MB * 1024 * 1024; an InputError becomes c.json({error: code, message}, status)); busy check: `const admission = getAdmission(deps)` (server/admission.ts, S2; call it at request time, never cache it) and `const gate = admission.canAccept()`; when !gate.ok respond 429 {error: 'busy', message, retryAfterSec: gate.retryAfterSec} with a Retry-After header BEFORE anything is stored (contract D-16); store the product with deps.assets.put(bytes, mime, {role: 'product-photo'}); if audio: text = (await transcribeBrief(audio, {meta: deps.meta, keywords: title ? [title] : []})).text, mapping BriefTooLongError to 400 audio_too_long and EmptyBriefError to 400 empty_brief (the film is NOT created); film = deps.films.create({aspect, brief: {text, transcript?: text when audio}, title, assets: [productRef]}); when audio, emit film's listener.transcript through deps.makeToolCtx(film.id).emit({type: 'listener.transcript', text}); bindDirector(deps) (once) and hand the run to the admission seam without awaiting it: `const queue = admission.submit(film.id, () => runDirector(film.id).catch((e) => emit an 'error' event))`; if queue.state is 'rejected' (the crew filled up between the check and the submit) set the film's status to 'failed', emit an 'error' event and respond 429 busy; otherwise respond 202 {filmId, queue}.

Create server/http/handlers/films.test.ts with makeTestFilm-style deps (build AppDeps in the test, a fake backend/director via vi.mock('../../agent/director') so no real run happens) and app.request with FormData: a valid typed brief returns 202 with a filmId that exists in the store with status 'new' and assets containing the product ref (role 'product-photo') and runDirector called once with that id; an audio brief (use makeFakeMeta transcript 'hello brief' and mock listener convert) creates the film with brief.text 'hello brief' and a listener.transcript event; a 61 s audio returns 400 audio_too_long and creates no film; an empty transcript returns 400 empty_brief; each validation error code from films-input is returned with its status; with a fake admission whose canAccept returns {ok: false, retryAfterSec: 90} the request returns 429 busy with a Retry-After header of '90' and no film is created; with a fake admission whose submit returns {state: 'queued', position: 2, etaSec: 200} the response is 202 {filmId, queue: {state: 'queued', position: 2, etaSec: 200}} and runDirector is not called by the handler itself; with one whose submit returns rejected the film ends 'failed' and the response is 429; with DIRECTOR_PASSCODE set a request without credentials returns 401 before any parsing.

metadata.standingRule: Offline-only PRD. Every story is implementable and verifiable with unit tests, recorded fixtures and the browser preview; nothing here spends money or needs network. Live and paid checks are listed in metadata.manualGates and run by the owner.
guardrails: Work offline. Tests use recorded fixtures and DIRECTOR_REPLAY=1. Never call Meta, Clippy, Ollama or any other network service from a story, a test or a script you run during a story. The only network use allowed is `npm install`.
Never commit, push, tag, publish to npm, deploy or change repository settings. autoCommit is off and the owner commits.
For engine behaviour (composition JSON, Player, timeline, layer kinds) read docs/engine/README.md before writing code; never edit or copy engine source.

Never edit anything under node_modules/. The engine `reacthub-pixitweenjs` is a dependency: if it lacks something, add a row to ENGINE-NEEDS.md (what, where, proposed API, workaround, story) and use a workaround or set notes to 'blocked: engine'.
Edit only the files named in the story's steps, plus their tests. Files under shared/ are contracts (specs/hackathon/meta/06-contracts.md): change them only in a story that says so.
Never put keys, tokens, cookies or personal data in code, fixtures, logs or docs. Fixtures are redacted: no Authorization headers and no data: URLs longer than 200 characters.
No real brand names, logos or real people's likeness in prompts, fixtures or assets.
Record only real results. Never invent measurements, latencies, prices or test output.
Do not add a dependency that the story or 06-contracts.md does not name. If one is truly needed, say why in notes.
Debug output goes to debug/<step>/iteration-NN/ (gitignored). Only curated, redacted fixtures are committed, under fixtures/<step>/.

A step that would call a paid or live API is written as a script that prints an estimate and exits unless `--yes` is passed (`npm run live -- <step> --yes`, one file per step under scripts/live/). Create such scripts; never run them.
Cost is recorded through ctx.ledger (from deps.makeToolCtx(filmId)); the Meta clients never write to the ledger. The ledger emits the cost event itself, so do not emit a second one.
The director talks to the film only through the S3a tools (runTool) and FilmStore; it never edits composition JSON by hand, except through the pure authoring API for the initial scene skeleton.
DIRECTOR_FAKE is read directly from process.env in fake-director.ts and is never documented in .env.example (production must not set it).
